title: Polyglot migration shims + codemods for v1->v2 SDKs and automated multi-repo changelog
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Objective: provide a low-friction migration path from SDK v1 -> v2 across Python, TypeScript, and Go by delivering language-specific compatibility shims, codemods to automate common API edits, canonical examples demonstrating streaming ergonomics and retry behavior changes, and a multi-repo automated changelog generator that surfaces deprecations and breaking changes for customers and internal release notes.

Background: v2 introduces ergonomic changes to streaming (evented stream vs single generator), stricter default retries (idempotency-aware), and some renamed/removed convenience helpers. Customers have reported friction when migrating large codebases that mix sync/async patterns and rely on streaming backpressure semantics. We also want a single source of truth for deprecations across repos (sdk-python, sdk-js, sdk-go, docs) to populate release notes and console migration guides.

Scope: deliver shims (lightweight runtime adapters) that route v1 call shapes to v2 behavior where safe, codemod scripts per language to rewrite common patterns (stream handlers, retry options, config field renames), full example repositories with before/after snippets, tests demonstrating backpressure and large-payload streaming, CI pipeline step that collects PR labels and commit footers to synthesize a consolidated changelog JSON used by the docs site and a release-notes Slack summary.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shims published for Python, TypeScript, and Go that translate the top 80% of v1 call shapes to v2 with opt-in flag
Codemods available in repo root scripts/ for each language (python/rust? no, python, ts, go) and documented usage in migration guide
Three canonical before/after example apps (chat streaming, embeddings batch with retryable failures, long-form generation with prefix caching) in examples/migration-examples
Automated changelog generator that aggregates PR labels and commit-convention footers across sdk-* repos and outputs a normalized JSON consumed by docs/release-notes
End-to-end CI job that runs codemod on a test workspace and asserts no runtime regressions on a smoke suite
Migration docs updated with clear deprecations table, mapping v1->v2 API examples, and recommended retry/backpressure settings
tasks: Design compatibility shim API surface and opt-in gate (assembly notes in design doc)
Implement python shim layer: packages/sdk_python/compat_v1_to_v2 (wrapper functions, minimal dependency surface)
Implement ts shim layer: packages/sdk_js/compat-v1 (preserve stream event emitter semantics where safe)
Implement go shim: internal/compat/v1 (ensure context cancellation semantics preserved)
Write codemods: python (lib2to3-style), ts (jscodeshift recipes), go (gofmt + regex transform with tests)
Author streaming ergonomics guide with blocking/backpressure examples and measurement harness
Add retry guide: explain idempotency token usage, default retry policy changes, and how to opt out or tune
Build changelog generator: multi-repo scanner that reads PR labels, Conventional Commits footers, and markdown deprecation annotations
Integrate changelog generator into release CI and docs site data pipeline
Create migration examples repo and link from docs + Console migration modal
